options.text: A single layer of graphite, one atom thick
A three-dimensional form of carbon like diamond
A mixture of carbon and iron

questions.explanation: Graphene is a single layer of carbon atoms arranged in hexagons, essentially one atom thick. It is the thinnest material known and can be thought of as a single layer of graphite.

questions.stem: Why is graphene an excellent conductor of electricity?

options.text: Because each carbon atom has one delocalised electron that can move freely

questions.explanation: Like graphite, each carbon atom in graphene forms three covalent bonds, leaving one electron per atom delocalised. These free electrons can move across the entire sheet, making graphene an excellent electrical conductor.

questions.stem: What shape is a buckminsterfullerene (C₆₀) molecule?
questions.explanation: Buckminsterfullerene (C₆₀) is a hollow sphere made of 60 carbon atoms arranged in pentagons and hexagons, resembling a football.

options.text: Cylindrical fullerenes made from rolled-up sheets of graphene

questions.explanation: Carbon nanotubes are cylindrical structures that can be thought of as graphene sheets rolled into tubes. They are extremely strong and can conduct electricity.

questions.stem: What is a potential use of fullerenes in medicine?

options.text: As drug delivery systems to carry molecules to specific parts of the body

questions.explanation: Fullerenes have hollow structures that can trap drug molecules inside them. This allows targeted drug delivery to specific cells or tissues in the body.

questions.stem: Why is graphene described as being extremely strong for its weight?

options.text: Because it has a very high density
Because it is an ionic compound
Because each carbon atom forms strong covalent bonds in a continuous hexagonal lattice
Because it is made of metal atoms

questions.explanation: Graphene's strength comes from the strong covalent bonds between carbon atoms arranged in a continuous hexagonal pattern. Despite being only one atom thick, these bonds make it stronger than steel.

questions.stem: Why can carbon nanotubes be used to strengthen composite materials?

options.text: Because they are flexible and dissolve into the material
Because they have high tensile strength due to strong covalent bonds

questions.explanation: Carbon nanotubes have exceptionally high tensile strength due to the strong covalent bonds between carbon atoms. When added to composite materials, they reinforce the structure significantly.
